newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump again, extending record-setting run.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump again, extending record-setting run.

text.p: Stocks staged another impressive rally Friday on still more evidence of moderate economic growth with little inflation, extending a record-setting run that started after Election Day.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 62.98 points at 6,375.98. The gain of more than 50 points triggered programme trading curbs on the New York Stock Exchange moments before midday.
In the broader market, advancers led decliners by a margin of 13-to-9 on heavy NYSE volume of about 309 million shares.
Early buy programmes contributed to the bulk of the Dow's gains, accounting for nearly 31 points, according to Birinyi Associates, a firm that tracks computer-driven programme trading.
The programmes accelerated a climb that has added about 295 points to the Dow since Election Day and, for now, appears to have taken on a life of its own.

"I think we're really in a phase where the market is going up because the market is going up," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist, at Oppenheimer & Co. "Momentum players are really in command right now."
Helping the rally were fresh signs that economic growth was moderating enough to ward off inflation without slowing enough to risk a recession.
The government reported a 0.5 percent drop in industrial production in October, the first decline in seven months, largely because of strikes that shut auto plants in Canada and the United States.
Business operated at 82.7 percent of capacity in October, down from 83.4 percent in September, reinforcing investors' belief that economic growth can continue with little risk of inflation.

"As long as interest rates stay low, the market can continue rising because there's no reason for people to sell stocks," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management Inc.

"The only thing that could cause problems is if the Fed decided to raise rates," he said, referring to the Federal Reserve, which held interest rates steady on Wednesday. "With capacity utilization heading back down it doesn't look like we'll see that happen."

International Business Machines Corp. was by far the strongest of the Dow components, surging 6-3/4 to 143-5/8 after Merrill Lynch analyst Dan Mandresh raised his 12-month price target on the company to $195 per share.
Russian telecommunications company Vimpel-Communications was the only issue to post a larger net gain on the NYSE, with shares jumping 8-7/8 to 29-3/8 in their debut on the Exchange.
ITI Technologies Inc. skidded 18-3/8 to 11-3/4 after the company announced its largest customer would cut back on orders during the first quarter of 1997.
The strength of the rally did not spill over to Nasdaq, however, with the Nasdaq Composite index off 0.57 to 1,269.79.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks added 5.38 to 741.26.
The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.41 point at 585.77.
